episodes.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can't trust AI CEOs
episodes.description: My guest today is Helen Toner, the executive director of CSET. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, where was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman. Since then, AI safety has entered the mainstream, as industry leaders have made increasingly dire predictions about what might happen if we don’t proceed more carefully or even slow down. Helen has seen up close what happens when safety commitments run headlong into commercial incentives. As she put it to me, if our hopes for the future depend on any one person being trustworthy, we’re in big trouble. Read the full interview transcript on The Verge. Links: The AIs

episodes.title: How Fast Should We Build Superintelligence? | Nick Bostrom
episodes.description: The question isn’t simply whether humanity should race toward superintelligence or stop. episodes.title: The Missing Layer for Personal AI | First Person Labs’ Ken Liu
episodes.description: AI agents are getting smarter, but every new agent still has to learn who you are. What if your preferences, priorities, relationships, and digital context could move with you instead? First Person Labs co-founder Ken Liu joins a16z’s Martin Casado and Joel de la Garza to introduce Second, a personal context layer designed to understand what you’re doing across your digital life and make that context available to the agents you choose. They discuss how Second can proactively connect information across conversations and applications, why protecting such personal data requires a different security architecture, and the longer-term vision of AI that doesn’t just respond to prompts, but understands enough context to know when and how to help. episodes.title: Can AI Learn to Improve Itself? | Recursive Self-Improvement
episodes.description: For decades, the idea of AI improving itself was just a thought experiment. Today, AI is already helping researchers at frontier labs run experiments, write code and test ideas faster. Mark Chen says OpenAI has built “AI research interns.” So how far are we from AI that can do the research on its own? In our first episode of Working Theory, a16z general partner Sarah Wang explores recursive self-improvement with two leading AI researchers: Mark Chen, Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, and John Schulman, co-founder and Chief Scientist of Thinking Machines Lab, and co-founder of OpenAI. They cover what RSI actually means, why research taste is so hard to teach, and why AI may be one of our best tools for solving alignment. episodes.title: Alex Imas & Tyler Cowen | AI Is Moving Fast. Why Isn’t the Economy?
episodes.description: AI capabilities are improving fast. But will the economy move just as quickly? a16z General Partner Erik Torenberg sits down with Google DeepMind economist Alex Imas and economist Tyler Cowen to examine how advances in AI translate into growth, jobs, wages, and productivity. They debate what it would take to reach double-digit economic growth, why bottlenecks and falling AI costs could slow the impact, and whether frontier lab valuations require much larger productivity gains. They also explore the “economics of intelligence,” including why the bigger shift may come not from smarter individual agents, but from AI agents learning to coordinate at scale. episodes.description: Raj Shamani just became the most-subscribed podcast on YouTube, passing Diary of a CEO and Joe Rogan. We sat down with the host of Figuring Out to learn how he got there, from selling dish soap to building India’s biggest show. Learn more about your ad choices. Visit megaphone.fm/adchoices
